open_points.subject: Randomly minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random identifier generation and the atomic collision check for records written by `functions`, `bindings`, `runs` and `effects`?
options: `store` mints every random identifier inside the write transaction
Each record-owning module mints identifiers and asks `store` to reject collisions
A separate lower-level identity capability owns minting
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and collision-check every random identifier inside the transaction that creates the record.

open_points.subject: Opening the store from installation configuration
open_points.text: The list runs from the bottom of the stack up: a module may know only modules on earlier lines of the list, never one on a later line, and modules on one line do not know each other.
open_points.question: How does `store.open_store` obtain `data_directory`, which is owned by same-line module `installation`, without either same-line module knowing the other?
options: `surface` passes the loaded data-directory value to `store.open_store`
open_points.default_guess: Have `surface` pass the validated data-directory value returned by `installation.load_installation` to `store.open_store`.

open_points.subject: Inputs of an owner-refused operation element
open_points.text: `runs` passes to `effects` the run's id, its pinned flow version and that the run has not ended, with every call about one of its elements
open_points.question: When `effects.decide_effect_approval` records `refused_by_owner`, how does `effects` obtain the exact StoredValue and SpooledFile input references required by M23, given that those element inputs are owned by `runs` and M24 retains only `input_digests` and a preview?
options: `runs` passes the element's input references to `decide_effect_approval`
M24 durably stores the complete input references
`effects` reads and reconstructs the inputs from run records in `store`
open_points.default_guess: Have `runs` pass the exact element input references to `effects.decide_effect_approval`.

open_points.subject: Authoritative source of a run's status and outputs
open_points.text:
The run's answer — status, outputs, and per flow output its value or the reason `skipped_by_guard` or `not_produced` (A13 rule 7) — is computed by `runs` from the trace when asked and is not stored; `runs.read_run` and every `runs` capability that moves a run return it. A run that rests carries only the outputs produced so far; the reasons appear once it has ended (A13 rule 7).

The element's records are the truth; the run's status and WaitingPoints M20 are derived from them and written by `runs` in its next store call.
open_points.question: Are M19 `status` and `outputs` authoritative stored run facts returned by `read_run`, derived cache fields that may lag, or ignored in favor of recomputing the answer from the trace on every read?
options: The trace is authoritative and M19 status/outputs are recoverable cache fields
M19 status/outputs are authoritative after each successful run-state write
Status is stored authoritatively but outputs and output reasons are derived
open_points.default_guess: Treat the trace as authoritative and treat stored run status, waiting points and produced-output references as recoverable advancement caches.
